validated_results.title: Circulating Folate and Vitamin B<sub>12</sub> and Risk of Prostate Cancer: A Collaborative Analysis of Individual Participant Data from Six Cohorts Including 6875 Cases and 8104 Controls.
authors: Endogenous Hormones, Nutritional Biomarkers, and Prostate Cancer Collaborative Group
validated_results.reason: Original pooled nested case-control analysis of prediagnostic circulating folate concentrations and incident prostate cancer risk with a target-specific estimate.

extraction.comparison_type: top versus bottom fifth of study-specific circulating folate concentration
extraction.design: nested case-control within six cohort studies
extraction.population: Men from six cohort studies (6875 prostate cancer cases and 8104 controls)

sample_size.excerpt: Circulating Folate and Vitamin B<sub>12</sub> and Risk of Prostate Cancer: A Collaborative Analysis of Individual Participant Data from Six Cohorts Including 6875 Cases and 8104 Controls.
sample_size.location: abstract, design sentence; total_n derived from reported group counts 6875 + 8104 = 14979

cases.excerpt: A study was performed with a nested case-control design based on individual participant data from six cohort studies including 6875 cases and 8104 controls; blood collection from 1981 to 2008, and an average follow-up of 8.9 yr (standard deviation 7.3). Odds ratios (ORs) of incident PCa by study-specific fifths of circulating folate and vitamin B<sub>12</sub> were calculated using multivariable adjusted conditional logistic regression.

effect_size.excerpt: Higher folate and vitamin B<sub>12</sub> concentrations were associated with a small increase in risk of PCa (ORs for the top vs bottom fifths were 1.13 [95% confidence interval (CI), 1.02-1.26], p<sub>trend</sub>=0.018, for folate and 1.12 [95% CI, 1.01-1.25], p<sub>trend</sub>=0.017, for vitamin B<sub>12</sub>), with no evidence of heterogeneity between studies. The association with folate varied by tumour grade (p<sub>heterogeneity</sub><0.001); higher folate concentration was associated with an elevated risk of high-grade disease (OR for the top vs bottom fifth: 2.30 [95% CI, 1.28-4.12]; p<sub>trend</sub>=0.001), with no association for low-grade disease.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Higher folate and vitamin B<sub>12</sub> concentrations were associated with a small increase in risk of PCa (ORs for the top vs bottom fifths were 1.13 [95% confidence interval (CI), 1.02-1.26], p<sub>trend</sub>=0.018, for folate and 1.12 [95% CI, 1.01-1.25], p<sub>trend</sub>=0.017, for vitamin B<sub>12</sub>), with no evidence of heterogeneity between studies.

p_value.excerpt: Higher folate and vitamin B<sub>12</sub> concentrations were associated with a small increase in risk of PCa (ORs for the top vs bottom fifths were 1.13 [95% confidence interval (CI), 1.02-1.26], p<sub>trend</sub>=0.018, for folate and 1.12 [95% CI, 1.01-1.25], p<sub>trend</sub>=0.017, for vitamin B<sub>12</sub>), with no evidence of heterogeneity between studies.
